description: Somos Neox-alpha, un equipo de seis participantes del evento local de Sevilla. En el reto Space Mission Design Game crearemos una experiencia clara, atractiva y educativa para explorar el diseño de misiones espaciales, sus decisiones, recursos y riesgos. Combinamos programación, software, desarrollo web, diseño gráfico, narrativa y pasión por la exploración espacial. Trabajamos en español e inglés.
summary: We built Mission Control Center, a 3D game in Unity where 1 to 4 players design, launch and run a space mission. You pick a mission (wildfire monitoring, polar ice, lunar ice, Mars climate, solar wind and more) and build the spacecraft: instruments, power, batteries, comms, computer, attitude control and propulsion. Every part costs mass, power, money and data, so you can't have everything. Then you choose a launcher and an orbit. With 4 players each one takes a role (Mission Director, Engineering, Science, Comms) and the launch only happens if everyone agrees. After launch the mission runs day by day with live telemetry and random problems you have to deal with, and you can also fly the craft yourself on a 3D solar system map. At the end you get a report explaining why it went well or badly. There's also an AI assistant in the game that answers questions in your language. The idea is that students and anyone curious learn how real missions work just by playing.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mission Control Center is a team game that covers the whole life of a space mission:

1. Define the mission: 7 missions with budget, minimum science, lifetime and deadline, plus 4 difficulty levels, a sandbox and a daily challenge.

2. Design the spacecraft: every instrument and subsystem has mass, power, cost, data rate and scientific value. Live panels show how each choice changes mass, energy, data and whether the launch is still possible. There is never a single correct answer.

3. Launcher and orbit: the launch is blocked if the craft does not fit; orbits (LEO, GEO, polar, transfer, capture) affect coverage, eclipses, communications and duration.

4. Team play: four roles with their own goals, and the launch needs the approval of all of them. Local network mode for up to 4 players.

5. Fly the mission: a day-by-day simulation with telemetry where everything is connected (a damaged panel means less power, then low battery, then blackout, then science stops). Incidents give you three options with different risks, and science only counts once its data reaches Earth.

6. Manual flight and 3D solar system map: optional orbital flight with Hohmann transfers, launch windows, maneuver nodes and assisted course correction.

7. Learn: guided tutorial, 32-term glossary, encyclopedia, "Why did this happen?" explanations, real NASA data, and a final report with score, achievements and what to improve.

8. AI assistant: an in-game chat using the OpenAI API (gpt-4o-mini) that knows the game rules and the current state of your mission. It answers in the player's language, and without an API key it still works offline using the in-game glossary and help.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It teaches the real trade-offs of space mission engineering (mass, power, data, budget and risk) by playing, and it trains teamwork and decision-making. It is aimed at students, teachers and anyone interested in space.

HOW WE BUILT IT

Unity 6 (C#). The game data lives in JSON files, and the simulation engine is deterministic and separate from the interface, checked with 198 rule tests plus automated in-game self-tests. Local multiplayer runs over TCP, and the game is fully translated into English and Spanish.

CREATIVITY

Instead of a static calculator, the mission becomes a living base where the crew walk around, get tired and argue over trade-offs, and every design leads to a different story with a final explanation of cause and effect.
